x: Ian Forrester, however, took the "A" team into the lead again and I think the local crowd were duly impressed with the fine form shown by our junior members.

Gregory won the 2 miles walk in 14 min. 12.4 secs., and this was our only other success except that our Junior team of Frank Kemp, Alan Law, Ian Forrester and John Benstead won the 4 x 110 yards Junior relay, beating Poly H. and the R.A.F., Halton, in 45.2 secs.
Maddicks, our young javelin thrower, who, with 14ft. 6in., did 43ft. 3¾in. Frank Kemp (11ft.) was second, with Ian Forrester (16ft. 6in.) third, and the scratch man, Gaworski, did 41ft. 3¼in.

There was also an open Schools 4 x 110 yds. relay, which was won by the Drayton Manor School in 48.2 secs. In the Junior match we had John Smith 1st in the 100, with Ian Forrester winning the 220 yds., Frank Wright won the 440, with J.
Jones and Ian Forrester, scored a good win in 2 mins. 6 secs.

The following evening, at Motspur Park, we fielded a team in a 1 mile medley relay and Ian Badiali gave us the lead over the half-mile stage, then Ian Forrester and Dicky Bartlett did the two 220's with "Jock" Cameron running the quarter, and we eventually finished 3rd.
Our members did well at the Charlotteville " open " meeting on Whit-Monday, and Ivan Mayers and Ian Forrester were 1st and 2nd in both the 100 and 220 yds. handicaps.

The relay proved a very convincing win for our very scratch team of Denis Merrett, Ian Forrester, Percy Luxon and Mal Ash. The long jump held by candlelight, proved a win for Percy Luxon with 21ft. 9ins. and I understand Mal Ash surprised himself by jumping 19ft. 4ins.

Carter, Ian Forrester and Clive ran well to finish second to the Poly, who had Shenton on the last leg, Clive hanging on for dear life for second place and gaining some valuable experience against top class sprinters.
